title: Are splay trees dynamically optimal?
question: Fix n ordered keys and an access sequence X. In the root-BST model, an access is served by rotations until its key is at the root; its cost is one plus the number of rotations. Let OPT(X) minimize total cost over offline executions, allowing an optimal initial tree. Is there a universal constant C such that, for every initial splay tree T₀ and every X, $\mathrm{cost}_{\mathrm{splay}}(X;T_0)\le C(\mathrm{OPT}(X)+n)$? The additive term allows an arbitrary initial configuration.

source.title: Splay trees are almost dynamically optimal

why: It asks whether a simple local adjustment rule can match every legal strategy with complete knowledge of the future. The issue is fundamental to instance-sensitive data structures: success would replace a growing competitive penalty by a constant for all access patterns. A counterexample would identify a limitation of splaying that its many separate locality guarantees fail to reveal.

title: Can exact weighted all-pairs shortest paths be computed in truly subcubic time?
question: Is there a constant $\varepsilon>0$ and a uniform randomized algorithm that, for every n-vertex directed graph with real edge weights and no negative-weight cycle, outputs all exact shortest-path distances in $O(n^{3-\varepsilon})$ worst-case time with probability at least 2/3? Use a comparison-addition real RAM: adding, subtracting, and comparing stored real values costs O(1), and standard arithmetic and bit operations on O(log n)-bit index words cost O(1). Unreachable distances must be reported as infinity. Arbitrary real-number encodings or unit-cost floor operations are unavailable.

title: The online Boolean matrix–vector multiplication conjecture
question: Given a Boolean matrix $M\in\{0,1\}^{n\times n}$, receive vectors $v_1,\ldots,v_n\in\{0,1\}^n$ one at a time. Output each Boolean product $(Mv_t)_i=\bigvee_{j=1}^{n}(M_{ij}\wedge(v_t)_j)$ before receiving $v_{t+1}$. Is there any constant $\varepsilon>0$ and randomized algorithm with total running time $O(n^{3-\varepsilon})$ and error probability at most $1/3$? The OMv conjecture asserts that there is no such algorithm. In this formulation the total includes preprocessing of $M$.

title: Is Exact Matching on general graphs in deterministic polynomial time?
question: Is there a deterministic algorithm, polynomial in the input bit length, that decides the following problem? Given a simple undirected graph G on an even number n of vertices, each edge colored red or blue, and an integer $0\le k\le n/2$, determine whether G has a perfect matching containing exactly k red edges. The algorithm must be correct on every input. No bipartition is promised, and no randomness or computational hardness assumption is allowed.

source.title: Exact Matching: Algorithms and Related Problems

title: Bipartite Exact Matching: deterministic polynomial time

The historical question asks for a deterministic algorithm polynomial in the ordinary bit encoding of $(G,k)$. An April 2026 preprint claims such an algorithm. This entry records that claimed resolution and its verification limits; it is no longer labeled as a confirmed open problem.

title: Do splay trees support deque operations in constant amortized time?
question: Start from an arbitrary binary search tree containing $n$ ordered keys, and perform $m$ legal double-ended queue operations. Insert-min creates a new minimum as the root with the old tree as its right child; insert-max is symmetric. Delete-min splays the minimum to the root, removes it, and keeps its right subtree; delete-max is symmetric. Is the total number of primitive pointer operations and rotations always $O(n+m)$, with a universal constant? This is Tarjan’s deque conjecture for the specified splay implementation.

source.title: Splay Trees, Davenport-Schinzel Sequences, and the Deque Conjecture

why: I include this because it tests whether one general-purpose adaptive representation can recognize a workload whose optimal cost is linear. The remaining gap is tiny numerically but significant mathematically: a proof would explain why expensive local restructuring cannot accumulate across arbitrary alternations of the two ends.

title: Can pointer-machine working-set heaps have constant amortized insertion and decrease-key?
question: Does there exist a deterministic online priority queue in the pointer-machine model below and an absolute constant C such that every legal sequence of M operations, starting from an empty queue, has total cost at most $C(M+\sum_{x\ \mathrm{extracted}}\log \Gamma(x))$? The operations are insert, find-min, decrease-key, and extract-min. For an extracted item x, define $\Gamma(x)=1+$ the number of insertions strictly after x was inserted and before it was extracted, including inserted items that have already been removed. An insertion creates a distinct item and returns its handle; decrease-key receives that handle and its new key. Require exact answers for all sequences; melding is not required.

source.title: Adaptive and Scalable Data Structures (Dagstuhl Seminar 25191)

why: This is a basic test of whether temporal adaptivity and cheap priority changes can coexist without word-level machine tricks. A solution would clarify a model distinction in a fundamental graph-algorithm primitive. The small remaining factor makes it a sharper structural question than simply asking for a faster heap.

title: Does splaying every BST preorder take linear total time?
question: Is there an absolute constant C such that, for every n and every two binary search trees A and B on the same n distinct ordered keys, searching for the keys of preorder(B), in order, using bottom-up splaying starting from A costs at most Cn? Define preorder recursively as root, then left-subtree preorder, then right-subtree preorder. Every key is searched once. Charge one unit per visited search-path node and one per single rotation; perform no insertions or deletions.

source.title: Splaying Preorders and Postorders

why: I include this as a concrete test of whether a local restructuring rule detects global order in requests without being told that order. It isolates a major obstacle in understanding adaptive search trees while avoiding the full freedom of arbitrary repeated-access sequences.

title: Two anticomplete paths with unrestricted terminal pairing
question: Is there a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that, given a finite simple undirected graph G and four distinct pairwise nonadjacent vertices a,b,c,d, decides whether G contains two vertex-disjoint paths with no edge between their vertex sets, whose four endpoints are exactly a,b,c,d? Any of the three pairings of the four terminals is accepted.

source.title: Computing disjoint paths, in Graph Colouring: from Structure to Algorithms

title: Does recursively splitting a splay tree always take linear total time?
question: Start with an arbitrary n-node binary search tree. A split operation receives a current component tree and a key x in it, searches for x, splays x to that component’s root, and deletes x, leaving its left and right subtrees as separate components. Is the total cost of every legal sequence of n splits O(n)? Count all searches, rotations, and constant-time component bookkeeping. The input to each operation supplies the component’s root handle; identifying which component contains x is not a separate search problem.

title: Can reachability diameter be approximated within a constant in near-linear time?

Here $n=|V|$, $m=|E|$, words have $\Theta(\log n)$ bits, and self-distances are included, giving D(G)=0 on an edgeless graph. The constant and the hidden logarithmic exponent are independent of G.

title: Can an acyclic subgraph preserve a constant fraction of the optimal reachable pairs?
